claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is governed by the development of chemical short-range order during annealing.
A critical level of chemical short-range order makes the high-temperature BCC phase thermodynamically unstable.
Al-centered local ordering is particularly important in reaching the proposed critical short-range-order state.
Reaching the critical short-range-order state nucleates a low-temperature phase.
Isothermal annealing between 800 and 950 °C for 1, 5, and 10 hours under inert atmosphere, followed by rapid quenching, is the proposed intervention.
Annealing permits local atomic rearrangements that increase chemical short-range order.
Exceeding a critical short-range-order parameter lowers the nucleation barrier for the low-temperature phase.
The lowered nucleation barrier allows the phase transformation to proceed.
The size and bonding effects of Al make Al atoms key contributors to the proposed local order.
Increasing annealing time and selecting an optimal annealing temperature will measurably increase the short-range-order parameter.
An increased short-range-order parameter will correlate with an increased volume fraction of the low-temperature phase relative to BCC.
As-quenched or minimally annealed samples should have a low short-range-order parameter.
As-quenched or minimally annealed samples should remain predominantly BCC.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to 800–950 °C, annealing durations up to 10 hours, and an inert atmosphere.
Transformation without a measurable increase in short-range order would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions say rapid quenching will freeze the high-temperature structure, whereas the predicted outcome expects the quenched specimens to contain an increasing low-temperature phase fraction. Quenching could instead freeze the structure present at the end of annealing, but the current wording is inconsistent.

The hypothesis describes the BCC phase as becoming thermodynamically unstable at a critical SRO threshold, while the mechanism specifically describes SRO as lowering a nucleation barrier, which is a kinetic effect. Lowering a barrier does not by itself establish thermodynamic instability.
